title: Screening for Hypertension in Adults
summary: The USPSTF recommends screening for hypertension in adults 18 years or older with office blood pressure measurement. Obtain measurements outside of the clinical setting for diagnostic confirmation before starting treatment. Grade A recommendation.

title: 2017 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
summary: BP should be categorized as normal (<120/80), elevated (120-129/<80), stage 1 HTN (130-139/80-89), or stage 2 HTN (>=140/>=90). First-line agents include thiazide diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and calcium channel blockers. Target BP <130/80 for most adults.

title: Resistant Hypertension: Detection, Evaluation, and Management
summary: Resistant hypertension is defined as BP above goal despite use of 3 antihypertensive agents of different classes at optimal doses, one of which should be a diuretic. Evaluate for secondary causes and medication adherence.

title: Standards of Care in Diabetes - 2024
summary: A1c target of <7% for most adults. Metformin remains first-line therapy. For patients with ASCVD or high risk, add GLP-1 RA or SGLT2 inhibitor regardless of A1c. For patients with heart failure, prioritize SGLT2 inhibitors. Individualize targets based on patient factors.

title: Classification and Diagnosis of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes
summary: Screen for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in asymptomatic adults with BMI >=25 (>=23 in Asian Americans) with one or more risk factors. Screen all adults beginning at age 35. If normal, repeat at minimum 3-year intervals.

title: Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes
summary: Screen annually for albuminuria and eGFR in patients with diabetes. Use ACE inhibitor or ARB for albuminuria. Add SGLT2 inhibitor for CKD progression reduction. Finerenone recommended for patients with diabetes and CKD with albuminuria on maximum tolerated RAAS blockade.

title: 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
summary: High-intensity statin therapy for clinical ASCVD (age <=75). Moderate-intensity statin for primary prevention in adults 40-75 with LDL >=70 and 10-year ASCVD risk >=7.5%. For very high-risk ASCVD, add ezetimibe if LDL >=70 on maximally tolerated statin, then consider PCSK9 inhibitor.

title: Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults
summary: The USPSTF recommends initiating a statin for adults aged 40-75 who have 1 or more CVD risk factors and an estimated 10-year CVD event risk of 10% or greater. Grade B recommendation.

title: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
summary: Use CHA2DS2-VASc score to assess stroke risk. DOACs preferred over warfarin for stroke prevention in nonvalvular AF. Rate control with beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers for most patients. Rhythm control preferred if symptomatic or early AF diagnosis.

title: Anticoagulation Decision-Making in Atrial Fibrillation
summary: Anticoagulation recommended for CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 in men or >=3 in women. DOACs (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, dabigatran) preferred over warfarin. Assess bleeding risk with HAS-BLED. Left atrial appendage occlusion for patients with contraindications to long-term anticoagulation.

title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
summary: For HFrEF, foundational therapy includes ARNI (or ACEi/ARB), beta-blocker, MRA, and SGLT2 inhibitor (GDMT quadruple therapy). SGLT2 inhibitors now recommended for HFpEF as well. Diuretics for volume management. Device therapy (ICD, CRT) per specific criteria.

title: Global Strategy for the Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of COPD (GOLD 2024)
summary: Classify by GOLD groups A-E based on symptoms and exacerbation history. LAMA or LABA for Group A. LAMA+LABA for Group B. LAMA+LABA+ICS for Group E with eos >=300. Smoking cessation is the most effective intervention. Pulmonary rehabilitation recommended.

title: Management of COPD Exacerbations (GOLD 2024)
summary: Short-acting bronchodilators (SABA +/- SAMA) as first-line for acute exacerbations. Systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 40mg x 5 days) for moderate-severe exacerbations. Antibiotics if increased sputum purulence. Evaluate for hospital admission based on severity.

title: Global Strategy for Asthma Management and Prevention (GINA 2024)
summary: Track 1 (preferred): Low-dose ICS-formoterol as reliever at all steps. Track 2: SABA reliever with controller. Step up/down based on symptom control and exacerbation risk. Biologic therapy for severe uncontrolled asthma (anti-IgE, anti-IL5/5R, anti-IL4R, anti-TSLP).

title: APA Clinical Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Depression Across Three Age Cohorts
summary: For adults with MDD, recommend psychotherapy (CBT, IPT, behavioral activation), pharmacotherapy (SSRIs or SNRIs as first-line), or combination. PHQ-9 for screening and monitoring. Combination therapy preferred for moderate-severe depression. Reassess at 4-8 weeks.

title: Screening for Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults
summary: The USPSTF recommends screening for depression in the general adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons. Screen for suicide risk in adults 64 and younger. Grade B recommendation.

title: Clinical Practice Review for GAD
summary: First-line pharmacotherapy includes SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram) or SNRIs (venlafaxine, duloxetine). CBT is first-line psychotherapy. Buspirone as adjunctive or alternative. Avoid benzodiazepines for long-term use. GAD-7 for screening and monitoring response.

title: Screening for and Management of Obesity in Adults
summary: Screen all adults for obesity. Clinicians should offer or refer adults with a BMI of 30 or higher to intensive, multicomponent behavioral interventions. Grade B recommendation.

title: Obesity Pharmacotherapy: AHA Scientific Statement
summary: Anti-obesity medications as adjunct to lifestyle modification for BMI >=30 or >=27 with weight-related comorbidity. GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide 2.4mg weekly) demonstrate 15-17% weight loss. Tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1) demonstrates up to 22% weight loss.

title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
summary: Classify CKD by GFR category (G1-G5) and albuminuria category (A1-A3). RAAS inhibition for albuminuria. SGLT2 inhibitors for eGFR >=20 with albuminuria. BP target <120 systolic when tolerated. Finerenone for diabetic CKD. Refer to nephrology for eGFR <30 or rapidly declining function.

title: AACE/ACE Clinical Practice Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Postmenopausal Osteoporosis
summary: Screen postmenopausal women >=65 or younger with risk factors using DXA. Treat with bisphosphonates (alendronate, risedronate, zoledronic acid) as first-line. Consider denosumab, teriparatide, or romosozumab for high-risk patients. Calcium 1000-1200mg/day and vitamin D 1000-2000 IU/day.

title: Screening for Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures
summary: Screen women aged 65 and older and younger postmenopausal women at increased risk (FRAX score >=9.3%). Grade B recommendation. Insufficient evidence to screen men.

title: Screening for Colorectal Cancer
summary: Screen adults aged 45-75 for colorectal cancer (Grade A). Options include colonoscopy every 10 years, FIT annually, FIT-DNA every 1-3 years, CT colonography every 5 years, or flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years. For ages 76-85, individualize decision (Grade C).

title: Screening for Breast Cancer
summary: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40-74. Grade B recommendation. For women 75 and older, insufficient evidence. Women with dense breasts or higher risk may benefit from supplemental screening.

title: Screening for Cervical Cancer
summary: Screen women aged 21-65. Ages 21-29: Pap smear every 3 years. Ages 30-65: Pap every 3 years, hrHPV test every 5 years, or co-testing every 5 years. Grade A recommendation. Do not screen women <21 or >65 with adequate prior screening.

title: Screening for Lung Cancer
summary: Annual low-dose CT screening for adults aged 50-80 who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years. Grade B recommendation. Discontinue once person has not smoked for 15 years or has a life-limiting condition.

title: Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule, United States, 2024
summary: Annual influenza vaccine for all adults. Td/Tdap every 10 years. Shingrix (recombinant zoster) for adults >=50 (2-dose series). PCV20 or PCV15+PPSV23 for adults >=65 or with risk factors. COVID-19 per updated recommendations. HPV through age 26 (shared decision through 45).

title: Pneumococcal Vaccination Recommendations for Adults
summary: PCV20 alone or PCV15 followed by PPSV23 for adults >=65, adults 19-64 with certain medical conditions (chronic heart/lung/liver disease, diabetes, alcoholism, smoking, immunocompromise). PCV15 + PPSV23 should be separated by at least 1 year.

title: Interventions to Prevent Falls in Community-Dwelling Older Adults
summary: Exercise interventions to prevent falls in community-dwelling adults >=65 at increased fall risk. Grade B recommendation. Insufficient evidence for vitamin D supplementation to prevent falls. Individualize multifactorial interventions.

title: 2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults
summary: Avoid benzodiazepines, anticholinergics, and sedative-hypnotics in older adults due to fall risk, cognitive impairment, and delirium. Avoid NSAIDs in CKD or heart failure. Review and deprescribe medications contributing to fall risk.

title: Interventions for Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults
summary: Ask all adults about tobacco use, advise to stop, and provide behavioral interventions and FDA-approved pharmacotherapy (nicotine replacement, varenicline, bupropion). Varenicline is the most effective single agent. Combination NRT (patch + lozenge/gum) is also highly effective. Grade A recommendation.

title: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions for Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adults
summary: Screen adults 18 and older for unhealthy alcohol use using validated instruments (AUDIT, AUDIT-C). Provide persons engaged in risky or hazardous drinking with brief behavioral counseling interventions. Grade B recommendation.

title: 2021 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain
summary: Use structured approach with pretest probability assessment. High-sensitivity troponin for acute presentations. CCTA or stress testing for stable chest pain based on risk. Dual antiplatelet therapy for ACS. Statin and BP control for secondary prevention.

title: 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack
summary: Antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel, or aspirin+dipyridamole) for noncardioembolic stroke. Anticoagulation for cardioembolic stroke (atrial fibrillation). BP target <130/80. High-intensity statin. Carotid intervention for symptomatic stenosis >=70%.

title: Screening for Thyroid Dysfunction
summary: Insufficient evidence to recommend for or against routine screening for thyroid disease in nonpregnant, asymptomatic adults. Consider screening in patients with risk factors: age >60, prior thyroid disease, autoimmune disease, type 1 diabetes, history of neck irradiation.

title: Guidelines for the Treatment of Hypothyroidism
summary: Levothyroxine monotherapy is standard of care. Dose 1.6 mcg/kg/day, adjust based on TSH every 4-8 weeks. Target TSH 0.5-2.5 mIU/L for most adults. Take on empty stomach 30-60 minutes before breakfast. Monitor TSH annually once stable.

title: Screening for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
summary: One-time screening with ultrasonography for men aged 65-75 who have ever smoked. Grade B recommendation. Selectively offer screening for men 65-75 who have never smoked. Grade C recommendation.

title: 2016 AHA/ACC Guideline on the Management of Patients with Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease
summary: ABI testing for suspected PAD. Supervised exercise therapy as first-line for claudication. Antiplatelet therapy (aspirin or clopidogrel). Statin therapy. Cilostazol for claudication if exercise insufficient. Revascularization for limb-threatening ischemia.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease
summary: Echocardiography for initial evaluation and serial monitoring. Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis: aortic valve replacement (SAVR or TAVR). Severe mitral regurgitation: repair preferred over replacement. Medical therapy for asymptomatic patients with serial monitoring.

title: Management of Venous Thromboembolism: A Clinical Practice Guideline
summary: DOACs preferred over warfarin for initial and long-term treatment of VTE (apixaban or rivaroxaban without initial parenteral anticoagulation). Duration: 3 months for provoked; extended for unprovoked or recurrent. Compression stockings not routinely recommended.

title: AGA Clinical Practice Update on Management of GERD
summary: PPI is first-line therapy; use lowest effective dose. Step-down to H2RA or on-demand PPI after 8 weeks if symptoms controlled. Long-term PPI is appropriate for erosive esophagitis or Barrett's. Address lifestyle modifications: weight loss, head elevation, meal timing.

title: International Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Treatment of Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis and Pyelonephritis in Women
summary: Nitrofurantoin 100mg BID x 5 days or TMP-SMX DS BID x 3 days as first-line for uncomplicated cystitis (if local resistance <20%). Fosfomycin 3g single dose as alternative. Fluoroquinolones reserved for complicated infections. Culture for recurrent or complicated UTI.

title: Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Preventive Interventions
summary: Screen for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35-70 who have overweight or obesity. Offer or refer patients with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions (structured lifestyle modification programs). Grade B recommendation.

title: 2014 Evidence-Based Guideline for the Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (JNC 8)
summary: Initiate pharmacologic treatment at >=140/90 for adults <60 and >=150/90 for adults >=60. Thiazide-type diuretic, ACEi, ARB, or CCB as initial therapy. For Black patients, thiazide or CCB preferred. For CKD, ACEi or ARB regardless of race.

title: AASLD Practice Guidance on the Clinical Assessment and Management of NAFLD
summary: Screen for advanced fibrosis using FIB-4 index in patients with risk factors. Lifestyle modification (weight loss >=5-10%) is primary therapy. Pioglitazone or vitamin E for biopsy-proven NASH. GLP-1 RAs show benefit. SGLT2 inhibitors under investigation. Resmetirom (Rezdiffra) FDA-approved for NASH with fibrosis.

title: 2019 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease
summary: Low-dose aspirin (75-100mg/day) should not be administered on a routine basis for primary prevention of ASCVD. May be considered for select adults 40-70 at higher ASCVD risk who are not at increased bleeding risk. Avoid aspirin for primary prevention in adults >70.

title: Prostate Cancer Early Detection Guidelines
summary: Informed decision-making starting at age 50 (45 for high-risk: African American, family history). Discuss benefits and limitations of PSA testing. If PSA <2.5, rescreen every 2 years. If PSA >=2.5, rescreen annually. Shared decision-making is essential.

title: Gout: Diagnosis and Management
summary: Initiate ULT (allopurinol preferred, start 100mg/day) for patients with 2+ flares/year, tophi, or urate arthropathy. Target serum urate <6 mg/dL. Colchicine, NSAIDs, or corticosteroids for acute flares. Anti-inflammatory prophylaxis when starting ULT for 3-6 months.

title: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain
summary: Nonopioid therapies preferred for chronic pain. If opioids prescribed, use lowest effective dose and shortest duration. Co-prescribe naloxone for patients at risk of overdose (>=50 MME/day, concurrent benzodiazepines, history of overdose). Monitor with PDMP. Reassess regularly.
